Rashi on Chullin 54a:10:3.english: On the sciatic nerve - [They struck it] with arrows or with a stick.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:10:4.english: And killed [it] - That [the animal] would die from this.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:10:5.hebrew: אתו לקמיה דרבי יהודה - לשאלו על כך, שאם לקתה בגיד הנשה שלה תהא טרפה, אחרי שאנו רואין שהיא מתה במכה זו:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:10:5.english: They came before Rabbi Yehuda - To ask him about this: whether, if it was struck in its sciatic nerve, it should be a tereifah, since we see that it dies from this wound.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:10:6.hebrew: אלא מה שמנו חכמים - ולקמיה פריך: הא קא חזינן דמתה:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:10:6.english: Only what the Sages counted - And later on [the Gemara] objects: But we see that it dies!

Rashi on Chullin 54a:11:1.hebrew: מחו בכולייתא - מכין בחץ החיה בכולייתא מלמעלה, ומכוונים שאין החץ נכנס ויורדת למטה מן הכליות לחלל:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:11:1.english: They would strike in the kidney - They would strike the wild animal with an arrow in the kidney from above, and they would aim so that the arrow would not enter and descend below the kidneys into the [abdominal] cavity.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:11:2.english: And it died - It died of itself.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:11:3.hebrew: אתו לקמיה - לשאול: אם ישחטוה אחר המכה, מהו:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:11:3.english: They came before him - To ask: If they slaughter it after the blow, what is [the ruling]?

Rashi on Chullin 54a:12:1.english: That if one scatters medicine on it - If one scatters medicine upon it:

Rashi on Chullin 54a:13:1.hebrew: ניקבה הגרגרת - בלא חסרון איסר, כדמפרש:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:13:1.english: [If] the windpipe was perforated - Without a deficiency [the size] of an issar, as [the Mishnah] explains.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:13:2.hebrew: או שנסדקה - לארכה, וכדאמרן: אם נשתייר הימנה למעלה ולמטה:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:13:2.english: Or [if] it was cracked - Along its length; and as we said, [it is kosher] if [an intact portion] of it remained above and below.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:13:3.hebrew: נפחתה הגולגולת - העצם נפחת, ורואין אנו שלא ניקב הקרום:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:13:3.english: The skull was fractured - The bone was fractured, and we see that the membrane was not perforated.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:1.hebrew: זה לתוך זה - שסמוכין הן, ודופנן של שניהם אדוקים זה לזה, ובאמצעיתן הן נקובין זה לזה. ואם חזרו ונקבו במקום אדיקת דופנותיהן, אין הנקב נראה לחוץ אלא זה לתוך זה — כשרה, דהא להדדי נמי שפכי:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:1.english: One into the other - For they are adjacent [to each other], and the walls of both of them are attached to each other, and in their middle they are [naturally] open to each other. And if they additionally became perforated at the place of the attachment of their walls, [such that] the perforation is not visible to the outside, but rather [only] from one into the other — [the animal] is kosher, because they also empty into one another.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:2.hebrew: ניטל לחי התחתון - מעל הבשר, והסימנים מחוברים בבשר:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:2.english: The lower jaw was removed - [The bone was removed] from upon the flesh, and the *simanim* [the windpipe and the gullet] are attached to the flesh.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:3.hebrew: האם - מדרי"ץ של נקבה, שהוולד מונח בה:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:3.english: The womb - The matrice [womb] of a female, in which the fetus lies.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:4.hebrew: וחרותה בידי שמים - מפרש בגמרא (לקמן חולין נה:) שצמקה ריאה שלה בידי שמים, כגון שנבעתה מקול רעם וברקים. חרותה — קשה כחריות דקל. ובגמ' (שם) מפרש: מנא ידיע אם בידי שמים, אם בידי אדם:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:4.english: And [if its lung] shriveled by the hand of Heaven - It explains in the Gemara (below, Chullin 55b) that its lung shriveled by the hand of Heaven, such as when it was frightened by the sound of thunder and lightning. [The word] ḥaruta [means] hard like palm branches. And in the Gemara (there) it explains: How is it known whether [it was] by the hand of Heaven or whether [it was] by the hand of man?

Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:5.hebrew: הגלודה - שניטל עורה, או מחמת שחין או מחמת מלאכה, ולא נשתייר כלום. ובגמ' (שם) מפרש כמה ישאר מן העור ותהא כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:14:5.english: The flayed [animal] - [An animal] whose hide was removed, either due to boils or due to work, and nothing remained. And in the Gemara (there), it explains how much of the hide must remain for it to be kosher.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:15:1.hebrew: כל היכא דתני אלו, מיעוטא משמע — אלו ותו לא:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:15:1.english: Wherever [the tanna] teaches “these,” it implies an exclusion: these, and no more.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:16:2.english: And taught: “This is the principle” - To include those [cases] that he did not teach.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:1:1.hebrew: וושט נקובתו במשהו - תנן (לעיל חולין דף מב.), הלכך דרוסתו נמי פשיטא לי דבמשהו:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:1:1.english: And [regarding] the gullet, its perforation is in any amount - We learned [in a mishna] (above, Chullin 42a); therefore, [the rule regarding] its clawing is also obvious to me that [it is] in any amount.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:1:2.english: The windpipe, its perforation [is] the size of an issar - We learned [this] in a mishna.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:1:3.hebrew: דרוסתו בכמה - כמה רוחב צריך להאדים:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:1:3.english: If clawed, what amount - [How much] width must redden?

Rashi on Chullin 54a:1:4.hebrew: אחד זה ואחד זה - וושט וקנה, דרוסתו במשהו:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:1:4.english: Both this and that - [The] gullet and [the] windpipe — its clawing [renders it a tereifa] in any amount.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:1:5.hebrew: מאי טעמא זיהרא מיקלא קלי ואזיל - גרסינן:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:1:5.english: What is the reason? The venom burns continuously - This is our reading.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:2:1.english: Rav would rule concerning it - Rav was accustomed to rule that it requires inspection from the hollow to the thigh.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:3:1.hebrew: כפא דידא - של יד, דהיינו עצם רחבה של כתף — אשפלדו"ן בלע"ז:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:3:1.english: The hollow of the foreleg - [The hollow] of the foreleg, that is, the broad bone of the shoulder — espaldon in Old French.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:3:2.hebrew: עד אטמא - הירך, דהיינו כנגד בני מעיים — דריאה וכבד נמי מיקרו בני מעיים לקמן (חולין דף נו:) גבי נחמרו בני מעיה:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:3:2.english: To the thigh - The thigh; that is, "opposite the internal organs," for the lung and liver are also called "internal organs" below (Chullin 56b) in connection with "its internal organs were scorched."

Rashi on Chullin 54a:3:3.hebrew: כפא דמוחא - כף הגולגולת, דהיינו כל החלל, ואף כנגד הסימנים:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:3:3.english: The hollow of the brain - The hollow of the skull; that is, [the inspection covers] the entire cavity [of the body], and even opposite the organs of slaughter [the simanim].

Rashi on Chullin 54a:4:1.english: Who is Rav, and who is Rav - Who is this Rav that they mention before us all the time?

Rashi on Chullin 54a:5:1.hebrew: ולא נהירא ליה - אין אתה זכור מי הוא? והלא ראיתי, קודם שהלך לבבל, שהיה משמש את הנשיא:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:5:1.english: Is it not clear to him - Do you not remember who he is? Why, I saw, before he went to Babylonia, that he was serving the Nasi [Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi].

Rashi on Chullin 54a:5:2.hebrew: בישיבה - הוא היה יושב ואני עומד, שהיה חשוב ממני:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:5:2.english: While sitting - He would sit and I would stand, as he was more distinguished than me.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:5:3.english: And who was greater - In what was he greater?

Rashi on Chullin 54a:5:4.english: In all [things] - In Torah and in piety.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:6:1.hebrew: פתח ר"ל ואמר - נהירא לי, וזכור הוא לטוב:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:6:1.english: Reish Lakish began and said - [It is] clear to me, and he is remembered for good.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:6:2.hebrew: שמוטה ושחוטה - נמצאת גרגרת שמוטה ושחוטה, ואין ידוע אם קודם שחיטה נשמטה:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:6:2.english: Dislocated and slaughtered - [Where] the windpipe was found dislocated and slaughtered, and it is not known whether it became dislocated before slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 54a:6:3.hebrew: כשרה - שאם נשמטה תחלה, היתה יורדת למטה, ושוב אינה נשחטת:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:6:3.english: [It is] kosher - For if it had become dislocated first, it would have slipped down, and then could not be slaughtered.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:7:1.hebrew: ויקיף - יחתכנה במקום אחר. אם דומין מראיהן של חתכים — טרפה, דהואיל ודומין י"ל שאף חתך הראשון לאחר עיקור נעשה:
Rashi on Chullin 54a:7:1.english: And compare - He shall cut it in another place. If the appearance of the cuts is similar, [the animal is] a tereifa, for since they are similar, it can be said that the first cut as well was made after dislocation.

Rashi on Chullin 54a:9:1.english: Seven halakhot - [These are taught] at the beginning of our chapter (Chullin 42b).

Tosafot on Chullin 54a:13:1.hebrew: ואלו כשרות בבהמה - כולהו צריכי, כדפרישנא בריש פירקין (חולין דף מב. ד״ה ניקב):
Tosafot on Chullin 54a:13:1.english: "And these are kosher in an animal" - All of them are necessary, as we explained at the beginning of our chapter (Chullin 42a, s.v. Nikav).

Tosafot on Chullin 54a:3:1.hebrew: אילימא כפא דידא היינו כנגד בני מעים - פירש הקונטרס: כפא דידא — עצם רחב של כתף, שקורין אשפלדו"ן בלע"ז; עד אטמא — הירך, דהיינו כנגד בני מעיים, דריאה וכבד נמי מיקרו בני מעיים לקמן (חולין דף נו:) גבי נחמרו בני מעיים. וקשה לפירושו: דנהי דבלשון משנה וברייתא הוו בכלל בני מעיים, בלשון אמוראי לא הוו בכלל, כדמוכח לעיל (חולין דף נא:) גבי נפולה, דקאמר אמימר: "נפולה שאמרו צריכה בדיקה כנגד בני מעים", ומר זוטרא מוסיף: "כנגד כל החלל", משמע דלא מיקרי בני מעיים אלא כרס ודקין, ואתא מר זוטרא לאוסופי עד כנגד הדפנות, כגון ריאה ולב וכבד וקורקבן; ובתר הכי בעי רב הונא: "נגד הסימנין מאי?", ואמר ליה רב אשי דקשין הן אצל נפילה. וכן לעיל (חולין דף נג:), דקאמר שמואל: "דרוסה שאמרו צריכה בדיקה כנגד בני מעיים", ואח"כ מוסיף רב חנן בר רבא משמיה דרב: "כל החלל". ונראה דכפא דידא דהכא — מסוף כפא דידא עד אטמא, דאין בכלל זה אלא כרס ודקין, ולהכי פריך: "היינו כנגד בני מעיים". והא דלא משני: "מתחלת כפא", שבא להוסיף אף ריאה וכבד — משום דמשמע ליה כפא סוף כפא, וגם הוה ליה למנקט "כנגד כל החלל", וגם ניחא ליה למימר "מכפא דמוחא", כדשמעינן ליה לרב לעיל (שם), דקאמר צריכה בדיקה נגד כל החלל ואפילו בסימנין:
Tosafot on Chullin 54a:3:1.english: If we say [that it is] the hollow of the foreleg, that is adjacent to the intestines - Rashi explained: "The hollow of the foreleg" — the broad bone of the shoulder, which is called espaldon in the vernacular; "to the thigh" — the thigh, which is [the area] adjacent to the intestines, for the lungs and liver are also called benei me'ayim [internal organs] later on (56b) regarding "its benei me'ayim were scorched". And this explanation is difficult: for granted that in the language of the Mishnah and the Baraita they are included in benei me'ayim, in the language of the Amoraim they are not included, as is proven above (51b) regarding a fallen animal, where Ameimar said: "A fallen animal about which [the Sages] spoke requires inspection adjacent to the benei me'ayim," and Mar Zutra adds: "Adjacent to the entire cavity." This implies that only the stomach and intestines are called benei me'ayim, and Mar Zutra came to add up to adjacent to the ribs [i.e., the thoracic cavity], such as the lungs, heart, liver, and gizzard; and after that, Rav Huna asks: "What is [the law regarding inspecting] adjacent to the simanim [the trachea and esophagus]?" And Rav Ashi said to him that they are tough with respect to a fall. And similarly above (53b), where Shmuel said: "A clawed animal about which [the Sages] spoke requires inspection adjacent to the benei me'ayim," and afterwards Rav Ḥanan bar Rava adds in the name of Rav: "The entire cavity." And it appears that "the hollow of the foreleg" here [means] from the end of the hollow of the foreleg until the thigh, for this includes nothing other than the stomach and intestines; and for this reason [the Gemara] objects: "That is adjacent to the intestines!" And as for why [the Gemara] does not resolve [it by suggesting that it means] "from the beginning of the hollow," which comes to add even the lungs and liver — [that is] because "hollow" implies to it the end of the hollow; and furthermore, [if it meant that,] it should have used the expression "adjacent to the entire cavity"; and furthermore, it preferred to say "from the hollow of the brain" [i.e., the skull], just as we heard Rav [say] above (ibid.), where he said: It requires inspection adjacent to the entire cavity, and even at the simanim.

Tosafot on Chullin 54a:7:1.hebrew: יביא ויקיף - יחתוך סימן זה עצמו שנשחט במקום אחר. אם דומה מראית של חתכים — טרפה, דהואיל ודומין, י"ל שאף חתך הראשון אחר עיקור נעשה. וההיא דפ"ב (לעיל חולין כח.), דשחט את הוושט ונמצאת גרגרת שמוטה — זה היה מעשה ואמרו: "כל ספק בשחיטה פסולה" — אין יכול להקיף על ידי שיחתוך הוושט עדיין במקום אחר, דממה נפשך לא יהו דומין החתוכין זה לזה, אפילו נשמטה הגרגרת קודם שחיטה, דאותה שעה היה עדיין חיות בוושט ועכשיו אין בו חיות כלל. וא"ת: ויביא עוף אחר וישחוט בו את הוושט, ואח"כ ישמוט את הגרגרת, ויראה אם מראיהן של השמוטות הללו שוין? וי"ל, דאין מקיפין אלא באותו עוף עצמו או באותה הבהמה עצמה. ולמאי דגרסינן כאן בספרים "יביא בהמה אחרת ויקיף" — קשה:
Tosafot on Chullin 54a:7:1.english: One should bring and compare - He should cut this very same organ [of slaughter] that was slaughtered, at another spot. If the appearance of the cuts is similar, [the animal is] a tereifah, since, as they are similar, it can be said that the first cut was also made after [the] dislocation [occurred]. And as for that [case] in the second chapter (above, Chullin 28a), where someone slaughtered the esophagus and the windpipe was found dislocated — such an incident occurred, and they said: "Any uncertainty in [the validity of] slaughter renders [it] invalid" — he cannot compare [them] by cutting the esophagus again at another spot, because either way, the cuts would not be similar to one another, even if the windpipe had been dislocated before slaughter, since at that time there was still vitality in the esophagus, whereas now there is no vitality in it at all. And if you should say: Then let him bring another bird, and slaughter the esophagus in it, and afterward dislocate the windpipe, and see whether the appearances of these dislocations are identical? One can say: One compares only within that same bird itself, or within that same animal itself. But according to what we read here in the books, "Let him bring another animal and compare," it is difficult.
